clue.text: Question family of pantomime coachmaker

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: An inquiry into the relatives of the man who built carriages for a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Cinderella pantomime, a British Christmas stage show, the fairy godmother turns a garden vegetable into her coach.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the coach is conjured from this vegetable, so it is jokingly the maker of the coach.

clue.text: We are shortly in a shell equipped with energy

indicators.note: in tells us the contracted words are placed inside the shell

parts.note: a pod is the shell of a pea or bean
we are, written short, is the contraction we're, letters WERE

explanation.surface: A group of us tucked inside an armoured casing that runs on electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' marks a contraction: 'we are' shortened to its apostrophe form, with the apostrophe dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something driven by an engine or motor has been supplied with energy to work.

clue.text: It's not where one would expect to find a poorhouse

definitions.text: It's not where one would expect to find a poorhouse

parts.words: It's not where one would expect to find a poorhouse
parts.note: the street name for a wealthy residential area, where workhouses for the destitute would be out of place

explanation.surface: A remark about the unlikely location of a home for the destitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a nickname for any street lined with the homes of the very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mansions owned by the super-rich is the last place for a refuge for paupers.

clue.text: Contract for new equipment going round

indicators.note: the equipment word surrounds the letter for new, as going round says

parts.note: a kit is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A deal signed for fresh gear that is being passed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a verb here, as in drawing the brows together, not a legal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit the brows is to draw them together, so the verb means to tighten or draw in.

clue.text: Note isn't man-made

definitions.meaning: in music a ... is a note neither sharp nor flat, or the sign cancelling one
occurring in nature rather than being manufactured

explanation.definitionFit: A musical sign restoring a note's normal pitch, and also describing things produced by nature, not artificially.

clue.text: Turning in grave? It's sour

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is spinning in their tomb, and the mood is bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges the letters of IN GRAVE; the phrase 'turning in one's grave' disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: The acidic condiment made from soured wine is the classic sour liquid.

clue.text: Artist's vehicle goes over the ditch

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as artist is

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second, as goes over says

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
a dyke can mean a ditch or channel

explanation.surface: A painter's van drives over a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flemish painter is usually spelt Van Dyck; this anglicised form is also used, as in a Vandyke beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Van Dyck was a seventeenth-century portrait painter, here in the anglicised spelling.

clue.text: Fix on one's finger

definitions.meaning: to fasten something in place with a metal spike
the horny plate at the tip of a finger

explanation.definitionFit: A pin hammered in to fasten things, and the hard covering at a fingertip.

clue.text: Having a lot on one's plate?

definitions.text: Having a lot on one's plate?

parts.words: Having a lot on one's plate?
parts.note: the idiom for being busy is read literally as a large serving of food

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed with tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a lot on one's plate' means being busy; read literally it describes a big portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish serving of food means literally piling a plate high.

clue.text: A dart i.e. designed to spread out

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A dart, that is, made to fly outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the seven letters of A DART I.E.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to spread outwards in all directions from a centre, like rays.

clue.text: With good purposes, like Jack and Jill?

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme pair went up the hill to fetch water, so their aims were on the water source

explanation.definitionFit: Meaning well, and punningly having intentions directed at a water source, as the rhyme's two children did.

clue.text: This is why I didn't walk out

definitions.text: This is why I didn't walk out

parts.words: This is why I didn't walk out
parts.note: a reason for staying indoors rather than going for a stroll: wet weather

explanation.surface: An explanation for not storming off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walk out' suggests a protest or strike, but it just means going outside for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling water from the sky is the usual excuse for staying in.

clue.text: What cows are said to do in Essex

indicators.note: are said tells us the word for the cows' action is heard, not spelt

parts.note: cows feed on grass, which is to graze

explanation.surface: A question about how cattle behave in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Grays is a town in Essex, a county east of London; 'to do' simply completes the sense of what cows do.
explanation.definitionFit: Grays is a town on the Thames in the county of Essex, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: She's in with the fair maids

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as she is

indicators.note: in shows the name is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl has joined the group of pretty young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the name concealed across 'fair maids'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: A farmer endlessly nimble

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the farmer's name is cut off

parts.note: Farmer Giles is the stock British name for a typical farmer

explanation.surface: A rural worker who is never still and quick on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a traditional British nickname for any farmer; 'endlessly' removes its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nimble means moving quickly and lightly, which is what agile describes.

clue.text: Begin to jump

definitions.meaning: to make a sudden involuntary movement from surprise

explanation.definitionFit: To commence something, and also to flinch suddenly with surprise.

clue.text: Performed by Georgia with first lady in Ireland

parts.note: something performed has been done
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word lady

explanation.surface: A show staged with a woman from the American South and a leading woman, over in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' looks like a president's wife, but 'first' simply takes the L of lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of the island of Ireland, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Force out Tex drunk and rude

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Throw out the cowboy who is intoxicated and impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a drunken Texan; 'Tex' is just three letters to scramble, and 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to push or thrust something out through an opening.

clue.text: Runner William returned the pan

parts.note: a ski is a runner on which one slides over snow

indicators.note: returned means the name is turned back to front

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: An athlete called William came back with the cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but is the ski; 'returned' reverses TELL, from William Tell, to LLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying vessel with a long handle used for cooking on the stove.

clue.text: One is not fit to receive it

definitions.text: One is not fit to receive it

parts.words: One is not fit to receive it
parts.note: money paid to an employee who is off work because of illness

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is unworthy of a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fit' seems to mean unworthy but means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages paid to staff who are off ill are received only when one is unwell.

clue.text: End-product, a tool is available that's not liable for duty

indicators.note: End takes only the final letter of the word product

parts.note: an ax, the American spelling of axe, is a chopping tool
free can mean available, not occupied

explanation.surface: Once the goods are finished, a tool can be had that escapes import charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End-product' looks like one noun; 'End' takes the T of product. AX is the American spelling of axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods exempt from tax or customs charges are not liable for duty.

clue.text: A growth developing on the wild-pig

definitions.text: A growth developing on the wild-pig

parts.words: A growth developing on the wild-pig
parts.note: a skin lump on a hog, read as the name of an African swine with facial knobs

explanation.surface: A lump forming on a feral swine.
explanation.walkthrough: The African wild pig takes its name from the wart-like lumps on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: This African wild swine has knobbly growths on its face that give it its name.

clue.text: Fish losing colour?

definitions.meaning: a small sea fish of the cod family
turning pale or white, read as a present participle

explanation.definitionFit: A cod-like sea fish, and also, read literally, becoming white or pale.

clue.text: Theologian is found under a prickly shrub at the bardic institution

indicators.note: in a down entry the theologian's letters sit beneath the shrub, as is found under says

parts.note: gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion is discovered beneath a thorny bush at a poets' gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, goes below GORSE; a Gorsedd is a Welsh assembly of bards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorsedd is the Welsh society of poets and musicians that presides at the Eisteddfod.

clue.text: About to cut and munch

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: Ready to slice and eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'ready to', but 'About' gives C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to grind food steadily with the teeth.

clue.text: Produced a bloomer using lower mouthpiece

definitions.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, or moos, such as an ox
the lip is part of the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone made a gaffe by using the bottom part of their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'bottom' but means a mooing animal; 'bloomer' is not a blunder but a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland primrose with pale yellow flowers is a plant that blossoms.

clue.text: Slight legato effect

definitions.meaning: an insult or remark damaging to reputation
in music, a curved mark joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging insult, and the curved musical mark telling a player to join notes smoothly.

clue.text: Knotty problem of row placed on its head

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing the word on its head means reading it upwards

parts.note: a rank is a row, as in a line of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: A tricky question about a line of people turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: A knar is a knot in wood, so 'Knotty problem' is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl in a tree trunk, so jokingly a knotty problem.

clue.text: Borough left its mark on the resort

indicators.note: left means the word for a town division is left out

parts.note: Scarborough is a seaside resort in Yorkshire
taken as written, the town-division word

explanation.surface: A town district has stamped its character on a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough is an English seaside resort in Yorkshire; with 'Borough' left out, the first part remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left by a healed wound.

clue.text: Do they co-operate badly?

parts.note: people who work together in wrongdoing co-operate for bad ends, not poorly

explanation.surface: A question about whether a team works well together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' seems to mean poorly, but means for wicked purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplices work together in wrongdoing, so they co-operate for bad ends.

clue.text: Second person is said to be by the actor found in the churchyard

indicators.note: is said to be signals that the pronoun is heard, not spelt

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Someone addressed directly is reportedly next to the performer, discovered in a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Tree was a celebrated London actor-manager; the conifer is traditionally planted in English churchyards.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark evergreen conifer is traditionally grown in English churchyards.

clue.text: Old swimmer first parked the car'

indicators.note: first puts the fish's name ahead of the word for old

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly bather came along first and left the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old swimmer' suggests an elderly bather; the fish name goes first, then AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To garage a vehicle is to put it away in its shed, so this means parked it.
